thread:
maria (devex): Heads-up — running into a weird replay/duplicate-create issue with the Python async SDK when the server returns a 5xx after accepting the request body.
rajiv (sdk): ugh, can you paste a minimal repro? which endpoint and are you using idempotency keys?
todd (prod): saw similar in prod traffic last week, suspected client-side replay after socket close.
maria (devex): repro below (very small):
```py
async with RedwoodAsyncClient(api_key=KEY) as c:
    await c.post('/v1/widgets', json={'name': 'x'})
```
The server logs show two creates when it returned a 502 during commit. I didn't set any idempotency header.
rajiv (sdk): By default the SDK retries on 5xx for POSTs? I thought non-idempotent methods were excluded.
kevin (eng-runtime): The runtime sometimes returns 502 after body read but before commit ack — that’s the window. If client retries, server may reapply.
maria (devex): Right. The SDK default retry policy seems to consider connection failures vs application 5xx differently. Behavior: if we see a connection/reset, we retry. But if we get an HTTP 502 after body sent, the async client sometimes replays because it thinks request didn't reach server.
rajiv (sdk): Hmm — in our current impl the async transport uses a streaming request body. If the request body was fully streamed, we mark it as sent and only retry on idempotent methods or if user provided X-Redwood-Idempotency header. Looks like we have a bug where the streaming layer resets state on some exceptions and drops the idempotency check.
todd (prod): Can confirm: traces show request reached host and server processed create, then returned 502 from a downstream. Client library doesn't surface any header-based idempotency enforcement in docs for async.
maria (devex): Proposal: 1) make async client automatically attach an idempotency key for POSTs unless disabled (opt-out), 2) tighten retry decision logic to treat 5xx after request-body-sent as potentially dangerous and only retry if idempotency key present. Thoughts?
kevin (eng-runtime): +1 for conservative default: safer to fail than silently create dupes. But auto-attaching keys has compliance/telemetry implications.
rajiv (sdk): I like conservative retry heuristics. We can add an opt-in auto-keying flag on client init for now, and a warning log. Also will fix the streaming-state bug so the idempotency header check is reliable.
maria (devex): Also hitting typing/UX stuff: Async client types don't expose `.retry_policy` param in constructor in stubbed typing — mypy doesn't know it exists. People copy-paste from sync examples and are confused.
rajiv (sdk): Good catch. We'll update .pyi and docs. We should add an explicit field `auto_idempotency: bool = False` and type it.
todd (prod): Operational ask: can we emit a metric when we do an automatic retry on POST without idempotency key? Want to detect these dupes in customer traffic.
kevin (eng-runtime): add metric: sdk.replay.duplicate_risk with tags {method, status_code, auto_key_used}. We'll wire it into logs.
rajiv (sdk): Plan: (1) patch streaming-state bug (2) change retry logic to require idempotency key for retries on non-idempotent methods when server returned 5xx after body has been streamed (3) add opt-in `auto_idempotency` with clear opt-out and logs (4) fix typings and docs. I'll open a PR.
ci-bot: ci started — PR 4532: fix(async-replay): tighten retries + idempotency header handling
maria (devex): Awesome. Can you add a short note in the changelog and an example showing how to opt-in? Also mention tradeoffs (duplication risk vs fail-fast).
rajiv (sdk): Will do. Anyone object if we default the conservative behavior in next minor release?
todd (prod): No objection. We should also notify support to watch for customer tickets during rollout.
kevin (eng-runtime): I'll add server-side mitigation too: make create operations idempotent by default when X-Redwood-Idempotency present and improve logs to surface when downstream returned error after commit.
maria (devex): Thanks team — follow-ups: PR link in #devex, update docs, add metric dashboards. :thumbsup:
